transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

This is not normal cycling: a single click followed by a steady running hum can be normal, but repeated clicking every few minutes while the freezer softens means it is trying, but failing, to start the compressor. The most likely cause is the compressor start circuit — usually the start relay/thermal overload attached to the compressor — intermittently overheating or failing. Less commonly the compressor itself is becoming hard to start. Poor airflow or dust around the back can make either problem show up more often. 1. Check the socket first: make sure the plug is fully home and try a lamp or charger in the same socket. If the socket is intermittent or electrics trip, stop using that socket and have it checked. 2. With the fridge-freezer switched off and unplugged, pull it forward if safe to do so. Vacuum dust from the rear/bottom grille or accessible coils and leave a few centimetres clear to the wall. Do not remove electrical covers or disturb the compressor wiring. If it was very dusty or boxed in, overheating may be contributing. 3. When it next starts clicking, listen at the bottom rear. A short hum followed by a click, repeated every few minutes, points to the start relay/overload or, if that proves sound, the compressor itself. Keep the doors shut as much as possible and move vulnerable frozen food to another freezer or cool box if it is softening. If cleaning and ventilation do not stop it, this needs a refrigeration engineer: they can test the start device and compressor safely. It is usually sensible to test the relay/overload before considering a compressor repair.

Thank you. I've already tried another wall socket and it was the same, and the fridge is plugged straight into the wall with no extension lead. The click comes from the box on the side of the compressor at the bottom back, and the compressor feels very hot to touch when it's clicking. Is there anything else I should check, or does this need an engineer?

Yes — at this point I would arrange a refrigeration engineer rather than keep running it while it is clicking and the freezer is thawing. The hot compressor and click from its side-mounted box point to the compressor start circuit repeatedly trying and then tripping on overload. The most likely replaceable item is the compressor start relay/thermal overload. If that tests sound, the next possibility is a compressor that is becoming difficult to start, which is a more costly repair. One final owner-safe observation can add useful evidence: switch it off and unplug it, leave it to cool fully, then only inspect the outside of that box. A burnt-plastic smell, discolouration or distortion makes the start device especially suspect. Do not remove the box or disturb its wiring. An engineer can test the start device and compressor windings safely, and should test the relay/overload before condemning the compressor. In the meantime, keep the doors shut as much as possible and move food that is softening to another freezer or cool box.

candidates: Compressor start circuit overheating or failing (start relay/overload) (high)
Poor ventilation or dusty condenser area causing overheating (low)
